feasible.reason:
The proposal does not defend against the threat it names, and its vendor precedent is for a different physical channel.

1. Channel mismatch. The stated threat is alignment on the SPI frame plus content-dependent bus current/EM. pq1's trusted UI drives the NV3007 at 20 MHz (`secure/src/hw/spi_hw.rs:187-213`; 80 MHz splash only), so the content-dependent signal (MOSI bit pattern = glyph pixels) lives at the SPI bit rate, tens of MHz. The mask is a 10 kHz PWM (TIMER_PERIOD 16000 @ 160 MHz) whose duty is piecewise-constant for 100 us (DMA table) or 1 ms (today's SysTick path, `secure/src/main.rs:4337`). Relative to a 20 MHz bus burst that is a slowly varying DC offset: a high-pass filter or per-window mean subtraction removes it entirely, and the PWM edges at a known grid give the attacker an extra alignment reference rather than denying one. Alignment itself is on the CS/SCK burst, which no supply-side load can hide. Trezor enables `consumption_mask` only on T2B1/T3B1 (`core/embed/models/{T2B1,T3B1}/model.toml`), the vg-2864 OLED models: there the leak is the panel's pixel-count-dependent drive current, a per-row/per-frame (~100 us-ms) signal squarely in the mask's band, which is why `display_refresh` re-randomises. pq1's TFT pixel current is negligible and the AW99703 backlight is content-independent; the residual channel is the bus, outside the mask's band. The proposal's own `risks` field concedes 'different channel' and then still claims defence.

2. Part (1) is a no-op on pq1. `randomize()` already runs every ~1 ms from SysTick, so a 48.6 ms trusted-UI blit at 20 MHz already contains ~48 duty changes; one more at flush start is unmeasurable. Drawing it from `rng_strong` is also wrong: `rng_strong` does SE I2C round-trips (`consumption_mask.rs:140-147,174-177`) and must not be called from the display path during the PIN/seed wizard; the platform TRNG (`rng::fill`) is what the existing reseed uses and is sufficient. The PRNG-predictability argument is already handled by the sca-1 reseed; the real defect there is #831 (biased fail-open), which part (1) does not fix.

3. Part (3) requires a PCB change (PA6 is pin 16 NC on the 48-pin QFN) and is correctly flagged mixed, but the physics does not change: a GPIO load is capped at ~8-20 mA and the random-duty square wave is a low-frequency additive term, so even on the supply shunt it raises trace count rather than preventing extraction. The 'close the unmeasured caveat' TVLA step is blocked on the Scaffold<->U585 coupling, not on the resistor.

4. Priority P1 and cost M are wrong for what remains. The only genuinely useful piece is part (2) as a #831 fix (TRNG-fed table, no linear state to recover, no ISR reseed contending with signing's `DriverGuard`), which is P3 hygiene costing ~1 KB flash (relevant: the ui-px image is already 76,949 B over the slot) and 476 B SRAM, plus silicon verification that the SEC|PRIV GPDMA channel is NS-unreachable (#53 still open). The pq1 request line is TIM3_UP, not Trezor's TIM2_UP.
feasible.corrections:
Reframe, do not adopt as written:
- Drop part (1). Per-frame re-randomisation adds nothing over the existing 1 ms cadence on a 48.6 ms blit, and `rng_strong` must stay out of the display path (SE I2C traffic during the PIN/seed wizard). If a per-frame hook is wanted for parity hygiene, call the platform-TRNG-fed table refresh, bounded (119 words ~0.5 ms at HSI48), and never block the frame on it.
- Keep part (2) but file it as the fix for #831/#646, not as a display countermeasure: GPDMA1 channel in circular linked-list mode, request = TIM3_UP on pq1 (TIM2_UP on iota2), SEC|PRIV|SRC_SEC|DEST_SEC, table in secure SRAM refreshed from `rng::fill` in thread mode (removes the ISR-vs-signing DriverGuard loss that biases the reseed toward signing windows). Record flash delta against the already-overrun secure slot; add the GPDMA secure-channel NS-block to the #53 silicon list. Priority P3, cost S-M.
- Part (3): before any pq1 respin, measure on iota2, where PA5/TIM2_CH1 is on the Arduino header and a resistor can be hung on it today; run TVLA on a C10 sign with mask off / mask unloaded / mask loaded. Expect the loaded mask to be separable by high-pass filtering; if the bench confirms that, the honest outcome is to downgrade the `consumption-mask` ship-blocker fence from 'countermeasure' to 'noise source, cost-raiser only' in `nsc/mod.rs:695-718` and CLAUDE.md, not to add a load to pq1.
- The stated threat (content-dependent SPI leakage of secret rows) is not addressable by any supply-side mask. Mitigations that actually match the channel: keep MOSI traffic constant-shape (already done: every cell overwritten, CT glyph fetch), minimise and shield the panel FPC/trace run at the next PCB spin, and accept that trusted-display content is visible to anyone with physical access anyway; the secret-bearing frames are PIN entry and seed words, so the residual to document is 'bus EM during the wizard', with the bench item re-pointed at that.
- Cite the Trezor precedent accurately: OLED-only (T2B1/T3B1), per-refresh randomise defends OLED pixel current, no mask on TFT models; it is not evidence either way for an SPI TFT.

vendor-claim.reason: The precedent claim holds for proposals (1) and (2): Trezor's vg-2864 OLED driver calls consumption_mask_randomize() inside display_refresh (core/embed/io/display/vg-2864/display_driver.c:407-425, call at :417, guarded by `USE_CONSUMPTION_MASK && !BOARDLOADER`), and the STM32U5 backend is a 119-entry TRNG-filled table streamed by GPDMA1_Channel1 in circular linked-list mode on GPDMA1_REQUEST_TIM2_UP into TIM2->CCR1 at 10 kHz, with DMA_CHANNEL_PRIV|SEC|SRC_SEC|DEST_SEC (core/embed/sec/consumption_mask/stm32u5/consumption_mask.c:26-29,34-38,73-142; attributes :85-87, node SrcSecure/DestSecure :117-118). The feature is enabled only on T2B1 and T3B1 (core/embed/models/T2B1/model.toml:5, T3B1/model.toml:5; all TFT models T2T1/T3T1/T3T2/T3W1/D00x list it 0 times), both `display_mono`, so the 'OLED-only' risk note is accurate; no st-7789/ltdc_dsi driver calls randomize (grep over core/embed finds only vg-2864:417). Our repo evidence also checks out: the sole randomize() caller is the SysTick handler (secure/src/main.rs:4285 `fn SysTick`, call at :4337), init at main.rs:1415, no randomize in secure/src/ui/lcd.rs, secure/src/ui/px/lcd.rs or secure/src/hw/lcd_nv3007.rs, xorshift-driven duty at secure/src/hw/consumption_mask.rs:166-192 with reseed every 1024 ticks (secure/src/consumption_mask_prng.rs:46), 'A full DMA port is a follow-up' at consumption_mask.rs:20, the unloaded-pin admission at :41-51, pq1 PA6 `NC` at secure/src/board/pq1.rs:309; gh #831, #646, #53 are OPEN with the stated content. novelty='parity' is correct for (1)+(2). Not refuted; the corrections below name where the precedent is incomplete or misattributed.
vendor-claim.corrections: 1) Proposal (3) (a resistive load on the mask pin) is NOT evidenced as Trezor practice: the firmware repo gives no board-level info for TIM2_CH1/PA5 on T3B1 (core/embed/models/T3B1/boards/trezor_t3b1_revB.h has no mask-pin entry; PA5 appears nowhere; the only 'tune' commit 4b68431f7c 2024-08-02 changed SAMPLES 110->119 and TIMER_PERIOD 16640->16000), and no Safe 3 schematic is published (web search found none). Treat (3) as beyond-vendor-evidence, not parity; it is the pq1-specific experiment that would close the 'unmeasured' caveat. 2) Trezor's per-refresh randomize refills ALL 119 table entries from the hardware TRNG (`rng_get()` -> core/embed/sys/rng/stm32/rng.c:38-47 reads RNG->DR directly; it is the raw TRNG, not rng_strong) — i.e. 119 TRNG reads per display refresh, not one sample; the D-06 'bound it so it cannot stall the frame' risk is therefore larger than stated if the table port is done faithfully, and our ISR-side guard contention (#831: `DriverGuard` loser is the preempting context) must be re-examined for a thread-mode per-flush caller. 3) Trezor also calls consumption_mask_init() in the bootloader (core/embed/projects/bootloader/main.c:335-337) and kernel (projects/kernel/main.c:161-163); our FSBL has no mask — a parity gap D-06 does not mention. 4) The Ledger source https://donjon.ledger.com/lsb/006/ (CVE-2019-14354) supports only the THREAT (row-based OLED power leaks displayed content via a USB shunt); Ledger's shipped countermeasures (per ledger.com/blog/oled-vuln) are randomised screen-update physical parameters (contrast/supply/oscillation) plus inverted-pixel boxes — NOT a PWM consumption mask, so it is not a Ledger precedent for D-06. Trezor One's analogous 2019 fix is pixel-count equalisation `oledSCA`/`oledSCAInside` (legacy/oled.c:454-497, callers legacy/firmware/layout2.c:836, recovery.c:469, pinmatrix.c:51) — a content-side countermeasure complementary to, and absent from, D-06. 5) repo_evidence citation 'docs/hardware/evt-silicon-validation.md §9 (unloaded-pin bench item)' is misplaced: §9 (lines 908-922) has no unloaded-pin row; the statement lives in the §1 table at :175 ('must sit near/across the die supply to matter (§9)') and docs/security/red-teaming.md:99 ('§6.7 PA5 mask scope'); consumption_mask.rs:48-49 cites §9 for an item §9 does not contain. 6) Minor: proposal names `px::lcd::present_frame_ex` — exists as a private fn at secure/src/ui/px/lcd.rs:304 (present_frame at :297); `flush`/`flush_with_secret_rows` at secure/src/ui/lcd.rs:153/180. 7) Trezor's pwm_data table is a plain global (consumption_mask.c:29), secure only because the kernel/secmon runs in the secure world; the 'S-SRAM' placement in D-06 is our requirement, not a Trezor-specified one.
